The 82nd Golden Globe Awards, held on January 5, 2025, celebrated a diverse array of cinematic achievements. *   **Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language:** *Emilia Pérez* (France)
*   **Cinematic and Box Office Achievement:** *Wicked*

*   **Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama:** Adrien Brody – *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Karla Sofía Gascón – *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Kieran Culkin – *A Real Pain*

#### **Supporting Performance Awards**
*   **Best Supporting Actress in any Motion Picture:** Zoe Saldaña – *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Supporting Actor in any Motion Picture:** Clarence Maclin – *Sing Sing*

#### **Directing, Writing, and Composition**
*   **Best Director – Motion Picture:** Brady Corbet – *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Screenplay – Motion Picture:** Jesse Eisenberg – *A Real Pain*
*   **Best Original Score – Motion Picture:** Volker Bertelmann – *Conclave*
*   **Best Original Song – Motion Picture:** "El Mal" from *Emilia Pérez* (Clément Ducol, Camille, Jacques Audiard)

#### **Honorary Recognition**
*   **Cecil B. DeMille Award:** Ben Stiller

You are an orchestrator responsible for breaking down complex queries into smaller, more manageable sub-queries.
When you receive a query, analyze it and break it down into focused sub-queries that can be answered independently. 
Be aware that you can create new sub-queries based on the information you receive from the subagents, your objective is to be as complete as possible.
For example, for a original question such as 'who were the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, how old are each of them?' you can first ask the subagent to find the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, and then ask the subagent to find the age of each of them separately.
Use the delegate_to_subagent function to send each sub-query to a subagent that will search for information and provide answers.
After receiving answers from subagents, synthesize the information to provide a comprehensive final answer to the user's original query.

### **Multiple Award Winners**
The following films and television series were the standout successes of the evening, each securing more than one award:

*   **Emilia Pérez:** The night's big winner, securing **5 awards**, including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy and Best Non-English Language Film.
*   **Shōgun:** Swept the major Drama TV categories with **4 awards**.
*   **The Brutalist:** A major force in the film drama categories with **3 awards**.
*   **Baby Reindeer:** Dominating the Limited Series categories with **3 awards**.
*   **Hacks:** Won **2 awards**, continuing its success in the comedy television space.
*   **The Bear:** Secured **2 awards** for its performances.
*   **A Real Pain:** Earned **2 awards** in acting and screenplay categories.

---

### **Full List of Winners by Category**

#### **Film Categories**
*   **Best Motion Picture – Drama:** *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Director – Motion Picture:** Jacques Audiard, *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Female Actor – Drama:** Fernanda Torres, *I'm Still Here*
*   **Best Male Actor – Drama:** Adrien Brody, *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Female Actor – Musical or Comedy:** Demi Moore, *The Substance* (Note: Some tallies include Karla Sofía Gascón for *Emilia Pérez*)
*   **Best Male Actor – Musical or Comedy:** Glen Powell, *Hit Man*
*   **Best Supporting Female Actor:** Zoe Saldaña, *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Supporting Male Actor:** Kieran Culkin, *A Real Pain*
*   **Best Screenplay – Motion Picture:** Jesse Eisenberg, *A Real Pain*
*   **Best Animated Feature:** *Flow*
*   **Best Non-English Language Film:** *Emilia Pérez* (France)
*   **Best Original Score:** Daniel Blumberg, *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Original Song:** "Mi Camino" by Camille, *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Cinematic and Box Office Achievement:** *Inside Out 2*

#### **Television Categories**
*   **Best Drama Series:** *Shōgun*
*   **Best Musical or Comedy Series:** *Hacks*
*   **Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for TV:** *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Female Actor in a Drama Series:** Anna Sawai, *Shōgun*
*   **Best Male Actor in a Drama Series:** Hiroyuki Sanada, *Shōgun*
*   **Best Female Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series:** Jean Smart, *Hacks*
*   **Best Male Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series:** Jeremy Allen White, *The Bear*
*   **Best Female Actor in a Limited Series:** Jessica Gunning, *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Male Actor in a Limited Series:** Richard Gadd, *Baby Reindeer*

*   **Best Supporting Male Actor on TV:** Tadanobu Asano, *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on TV:** Jamie Foxx, *Jamie Foxx: What Had Happened Was...*

#### **Special Honorary Awards**
*   **Cecil B. DeMille Award:** Viola Davis (for outstanding contributions to the world of entertainment)
*   **Carol Burnett Award:** Ted Danson (for outstanding contributions to television)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount%2B "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_P%C3%A9rez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount%2B "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_P%C3%A9rez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sof%C3%ADa_Gasc%C3%B3n "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal "El Mal")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A9ment_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_%26_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18)

message.content:
The 82nd Golden Globe Awards, held on January 5, 2025, at the Beverly Hilton Hotel, celebrated the best in film and television from 2024. The ceremony saw historic wins and clear dominance by a few select titles.

### **Report of Winners by Category**

#### **Film Categories**
*   **Best Motion Picture – Drama:** *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Animated:** *The Wild Robot*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language:** *Emilia Pérez* (France)
*   **Best Director – Motion Picture:** Brady Corbet — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Screenplay – Motion Picture:** Jacques Audiard — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama:** Fernanda Torres — *I'm Still Here*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama:** Adrien Brody — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Karla Sofía Gascón — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Sebastian Stan — *A Different Man*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role in any Motion Picture:** Zoe Saldaña — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role in any Motion Picture:** Guy Pearce — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Original Score – Motion Picture:** Daniel Blumberg — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Original Song – Motion Picture:** "El Mal" — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Cinematic and Box Office Achievement:** *Inside Out 2*

#### **Television Categories**
*   **Best Television Series – Drama:** *Shōgun*
*   **Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** *Hacks*
*   **Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Television Series – Drama:** Anna Sawai — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Drama:** Hiroyuki Sanada — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** Jean Smart — *Hacks*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** Jeremy Allen White — *The Bear*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** Jodie Foster — *True Detective: Night Country*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** Richard Gadd — *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role on Television:** Jessica Gunning — *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role on Television:** Tadanobu Asano — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television:** Jamie Foxx — *Jamie Foxx: What Had Happened Was*

#### **Honorary Awards**
*   **Cecil B. DeMille Award:** Viola Davis
*   **Carol Burnett Award:** Ted Danson

---

### **Productions with Multiple Wins**

The following films and television series were the "big winners" of the night, securing more than one award:

**Films:**
*   **Emilia Pérez (6 wins):** Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language, Best Screenplay, Best Actress – Musical or Comedy (Karla Sofía Gascón), Best Supporting Actress (Zoe Saldaña), and Best Original Song ("El Mal").
*   **The Brutalist (5 wins):** Best Motion Picture – Drama, Best Director (Brady Corbet), Best Actor – Drama (Adrien Brody), Best Supporting Actor (Guy Pearce), and Best Original Score.

**Television Series:**
*   **Shōgun (4 wins):** Best Television Series – Drama, Best Actor – Drama (Hiroyuki Sanada), Best Actress – Drama (Anna Sawai), and Best Supporting Actor (Tadanobu Asano).
*   **Baby Reindeer (3 wins):** Best Limited Series, Best Actor in a Limited Series (Richard Gadd), and Best Supporting Actress (Jessica Gunning).
*   **Hacks (2 wins):** Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy, and Best Actress – Musical or Comedy (Jean Smart).

At the **82nd Golden Globe Awards**, held on January 5, 2025, several films and television series secured multiple wins. The musical film *Emilia Pérez* and the historical drama series *Shōgun* emerged as the night's biggest winners.

### Films with Multiple Wins
*   **Emilia Pérez (4 Wins):**
    *   Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy
    *   Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language
    *   Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture (Zoe Saldaña)
    *   Best Original Song ("El Mal" by Clément Ducol, Camille, and Jacques Audiard)
*   **The Brutalist (3 Wins):**
    *   Best Motion Picture – Drama
    *   Best Director (Brady Corbet)
    *   Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (Adrien Brody)

### TV Series with Multiple Wins
*   **Shōgun (4 Wins):**
    *   Best Television Series – Drama
    *   Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama (Hiroyuki Sanada)
    *   Best Actress in a Television Series – Drama (Anna Sawai)
    *   Best Supporting Actor on Television (Tadanobu Asano)
*   **Baby Reindeer (2 Wins):**
    *   Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television
    *   Best Supporting Actress on Television (Jessica Gunning)
*   **Hacks (2 Wins):**
    *   Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   Best Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (Jean Smart)

### Key Achievements
*   **Karla Sofía Gascón** (*Emilia Pérez*) made history as the first trans nominee in a motion picture acting category.
*   **Fernanda Torres** became the first Brazilian actress to win Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama for her role in *I'm Still Here*.
*   **Sebastian Stan** was a notable presence, winning Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy for *A Different Man* while also being nominated for his portrayal of Donald Trump in *The Apprentice*.

    *   Best Original Song ("El Mal" by Clément Ducol, Camille, and Jacques Audiard)
*   **The Brutalist (3 Wins):**
    *   Best Motion Picture – Drama
    *   Best Director (Brady Corbet)
    *   Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (Adrien Brody)

### TV Series with Multiple Wins
*   **Shōgun (4 Wins):**
    *   Best Television Series – Drama
    *   Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama (Hiroyuki Sanada)
    *   Best Actress in a Television Series – Drama (Anna Sawai)
    *   Best Supporting Actor on Television (Tadanobu Asano)
*   **Baby Reindeer (2 Wins):**
    *   Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television
    *   Best Supporting Actress on Television (Jessica Gunning)
*   **Hacks (2 Wins):**
    *   Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   Best Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (Jean Smart)

### Key Achievements
*   **Karla Sofía Gascón** (*Emilia Pérez*) made history as the first trans nominee in a motion picture acting category.
*   **Fernanda Torres** became the first Brazilian actress to win Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama for her role in *I'm Still Here*.
*   **Sebastian Stan** was a notable presence, winning Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy for *A Different Man* while also being nominated for his portrayal of Donald Trump in *The Apprentice*.

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount%2B "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_P%C3%A9rez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount%2B "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_P%C3%A9rez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sof%C3%ADa_Gasc%C3%B3n "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal "El Mal")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cl%C3%A9ment_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_%26_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Winners-19)

message.content:
The 82nd Golden Globe Awards, held on January 5, 2025, at the Beverly Hilton Hotel, celebrated the best in film and television from 2024. The ceremony saw historic wins and clear dominance by a few select titles.

### **Report of Winners by Category**

#### **Film Categories**
*   **Best Motion Picture – Drama:** *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Animated:** *The Wild Robot*
*   **Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language:** *Emilia Pérez* (France)
*   **Best Director – Motion Picture:** Brady Corbet — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Screenplay – Motion Picture:** Jacques Audiard — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama:** Fernanda Torres — *I'm Still Here*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama:** Adrien Brody — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Karla Sofía Gascón — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy:** Sebastian Stan — *A Different Man*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role in any Motion Picture:** Zoe Saldaña — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role in any Motion Picture:** Guy Pearce — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Original Score – Motion Picture:** Daniel Blumberg — *The Brutalist*
*   **Best Original Song – Motion Picture:** "El Mal" — *Emilia Pérez*
*   **Cinematic and Box Office Achievement:** *Inside Out 2*

#### **Television Categories**
*   **Best Television Series – Drama:** *Shōgun*
*   **Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** *Hacks*
*   **Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Television Series – Drama:** Anna Sawai — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Drama:** Hiroyuki Sanada — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** Jean Smart — *Hacks*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy:** Jeremy Allen White — *The Bear*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** Jodie Foster — *True Detective: Night Country*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television:** Richard Gadd — *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role on Television:** Jessica Gunning — *Baby Reindeer*
*   **Best Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role on Television:** Tadanobu Asano — *Shōgun*
*   **Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television:** Jamie Foxx — *Jamie Foxx: What Had Happened Was*

#### **Honorary Awards**
*   **Cecil B. DeMille Award:** Viola Davis
*   **Carol Burnett Award:** Ted Danson

---

### **Productions with Multiple Wins**

The following films and television series were the "big winners" of the night, securing more than one award:

**Films:**
*   **Emilia Pérez (6 wins):** Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language, Best Screenplay, Best Actress – Musical or Comedy (Karla Sofía Gascón), Best Supporting Actress (Zoe Saldaña), and Best Original Song ("El Mal").
*   **The Brutalist (5 wins):** Best Motion Picture – Drama, Best Director (Brady Corbet), Best Actor – Drama (Adrien Brody), Best Supporting Actor (Guy Pearce), and Best Original Score.

**Television Series:**
*   **Shōgun (4 wins):** Best Television Series – Drama, Best Actor – Drama (Hiroyuki Sanada), Best Actress – Drama (Anna Sawai), and Best Supporting Actor (Tadanobu Asano).
*   **Baby Reindeer (3 wins):** Best Limited Series, Best Actor in a Limited Series (Richard Gadd), and Best Supporting Actress (Jessica Gunning).
*   **Hacks (2 wins):** Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy, and Best Actress – Musical or Comedy (Jean Smart).

response:
This report tracks the versatile actors who maintained their momentum in the industry by securing nominations at both the **81st (2024)** and **82nd (2025)** Golden Globe Awards.

### **Overview of "Back-to-Back" Nominees**
A select group of actors managed to bridge the gap between two highly competitive years, often transitioning between film and television or continuing their success in a long-running series.

---

### **1. The Multi-Medium Performers**
These actors were nominated for different projects across the two years, often showing their range by moving between Film and Television.

*   **Kieran Culkin**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama (*Succession*)
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture (*A Real Pain*)
*   **Jeremy Strong**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama (*Succession*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture (*The Apprentice*)
*   **Andrew Scott**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*All of Us Strangers*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Ripley*)
*   **Colman Domingo**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Rustin*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Sing Sing*)
*   **Timothée Chalamet**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*Wonka*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*A Complete Unknown*)
*   **Jodie Foster**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture (*Nyad*)
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actress in a Limited Series (*True Detective: Night Country*)

---

### **2. The Television Powerhouses**
These actors remained at the top of their field, largely due to the continued success of acclaimed series like *The Bear* and *Only Murders in the Building*.

*   **Jeremy Allen White (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Ayo Edebiri (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Ebon Moss-Bachrach (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actor – Television
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Selena Gomez (*Only Murders in the Building* & *Emilia Pérez*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Dual Nominee: Best Actress in a TV series – Musical or Comedy AND Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture
*   **Steve Martin & Martin Short (*Only Murders in the Building*)**
    *   **81st & 82nd:** Both nominated in both years for Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy.
*   **Gary Oldman (*Slow Horses*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama
*   **Quinta Brunson (*Abbott Elementary*)**
    *   **81st & 82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy.

---

### **3. Limited Series & Anthology Stars**
These actors performed in separate high-profile limited series or were recognized for the same role as seasons spanned different eligibility windows.

*   **Jon Hamm**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Fargo*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Fargo*)

This report tracks the versatile actors who maintained their momentum in the industry by securing nominations at both the **81st (2024)** and **82nd (2025)** Golden Globe Awards.

### **Overview of "Back-to-Back" Nominees**
A select group of actors managed to bridge the gap between two highly competitive years, often transitioning between film and television or continuing their success in a long-running series.

---

### **1. The Multi-Medium Performers**
These actors were nominated for different projects across the two years, often showing their range by moving between Film and Television.

*   **Kieran Culkin**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama (*Succession*)
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture (*A Real Pain*)
*   **Jeremy Strong**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama (*Succession*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture (*The Apprentice*)
*   **Andrew Scott**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*All of Us Strangers*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Ripley*)
*   **Colman Domingo**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Rustin*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Sing Sing*)
*   **Timothée Chalamet**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*Wonka*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*A Complete Unknown*)
*   **Jodie Foster**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture (*Nyad*)
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actress in a Limited Series (*True Detective: Night Country*)

---

### **2. The Television Powerhouses**
These actors remained at the top of their field, largely due to the continued success of acclaimed series like *The Bear* and *Only Murders in the Building*.

*   **Jeremy Allen White (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Ayo Edebiri (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Winner, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Ebon Moss-Bachrach (*The Bear*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Supporting Actor – Television
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
*   **Selena Gomez (*Only Murders in the Building* & *Emilia Pérez*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy
    *   **82nd:** Dual Nominee: Best Actress in a TV series – Musical or Comedy AND Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture
*   **Steve Martin & Martin Short (*Only Murders in the Building*)**
    *   **81st & 82nd:** Both nominated in both years for Best Actor in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy.
*   **Gary Oldman (*Slow Horses*)**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama
    *   **82nd:** Winner, Best Actor in a TV Series – Drama
*   **Quinta Brunson (*Abbott Elementary*)**
    *   **81st & 82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Musical or Comedy.

---

### **3. Limited Series & Anthology Stars**
These actors performed in separate high-profile limited series or were recognized for the same role as seasons spanned different eligibility windows.

*   **Jon Hamm**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Fargo*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actor in a Limited Series (*Fargo*)
*   **Brie Larson**
    *   **81st:** Nominee, Best Actress in a Limited Series (*Lessons in Chemistry*)
    *   **82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a Limited Series (*Lessons in Chemistry*)
*   **Imelda Staunton (*The Crown*)**
    *   **81st & 82nd:** Nominee, Best Actress in a TV Series – Drama (final seasons).

**LOS ANGELES**, December 9, 2024 – Today, the Golden Globes® announced the nominees for the 82nd Annual Golden Globes®, which will air live on Sunday, January 5, 2025, at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ in the U.S. (live and on-demand for Paramount+ with SHOWTIME subscribers, or on-demand for Paramount+ Essential subscribers the day after the special airs).* **Mindy Kaling** and **Morris Chestnut** presented nominees for each of the 27 award categories at a press conference at the Beverly Hilton.

This report details the actors and actresses who achieved the prestigious feat of being nominated for Golden Globe Awards in two consecutive years: the 81st ceremony (2024) and the 82nd ceremony (2025).

A total of **16 performers** managed to secure nominations across both years, spanning various categories in both Motion Pictures and Television.

### **1. Multiple Nominees in Both Years**
Several stars were not just nominated in both years, but earned multiple nods in a single year or across categories.

*   **Selena Gomez:** A standout over the two-year period. In 2024, she was nominated for TV Comedy Actress (*Only Murders in the Building*). In 2025, she earned a double nomination: once for the same TV role and another for Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture (*Emilia Pérez*).
*   **Emma Stone:** After winning Best Actress (Musical/Comedy) and being nominated for TV Drama Actress in 2024 (*Poor Things* and *The Curse*), she returned in 2025 with a nomination for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy for *Kinds of Kindness*.

### **2. Consistent Television Honors**
The following actors were nominated for the exact same role in both 2024 and 2025, showcasing the sustained critical acclaim of their series:

*   **Jeremy Allen White** (*The Bear*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Ayo Edebiri** (*The Bear*) - Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Quinta Brunson** (*Abbott Elementary*) - Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Steve Martin** (*Only Murders in the Building*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Martin Short** (*Only Murders in the Building*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Gary Oldman** (*Slow Horses*) - Best Actor in a Drama Series.
*   **Keri Russell** (*The Diplomat*) - Best Actress in a Drama Series.
*   **Jason Segel** (*Shrinking*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.

### **3. Performers Crossing Over (Film & TV)**
These actors received nominations in both years but for different projects, often moving between the big and small screens:

*   **Timothée Chalamet:** Nominated for *Wonka* (Film Comedy) in 2024 and *A Complete Unknown* (Film Drama) in 2025.
*   **Colman Domingo:** Nominated for *Rustin* (Film Drama) in 2024 and *Sing Sing* (Film Drama) in 2025.

*   **Jeremy Strong:** Nominated for *Succession* (TV Drama) in 2024 and *The Apprentice* (Supporting Film Actor) in 2025.

**LOS ANGELES**, December 9, 2024 – Today, the Golden Globes® announced the nominees for the 82nd Annual Golden Globes®, which will air live on Sunday, January 5, 2025, at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ in the U.S. (live and on-demand for Paramount+ with SHOWTIME subscribers, or on-demand for Paramount+ Essential subscribers the day after the special airs).* **Mindy Kaling** and **Morris Chestnut** presented nominees for each of the 27 award categories at a press conference at the Beverly Hilton.

This report details the actors and actresses who achieved the prestigious feat of being nominated for Golden Globe Awards in two consecutive years: the 81st ceremony (2024) and the 82nd ceremony (2025).

A total of **16 performers** managed to secure nominations across both years, spanning various categories in both Motion Pictures and Television.

### **1. Multiple Nominees in Both Years**
Several stars were not just nominated in both years, but earned multiple nods in a single year or across categories.

*   **Selena Gomez:** A standout over the two-year period. In 2024, she was nominated for TV Comedy Actress (*Only Murders in the Building*). In 2025, she earned a double nomination: once for the same TV role and another for Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture (*Emilia Pérez*).
*   **Emma Stone:** After winning Best Actress (Musical/Comedy) and being nominated for TV Drama Actress in 2024 (*Poor Things* and *The Curse*), she returned in 2025 with a nomination for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy for *Kinds of Kindness*.

### **2. Consistent Television Honors**
The following actors were nominated for the exact same role in both 2024 and 2025, showcasing the sustained critical acclaim of their series:

*   **Jeremy Allen White** (*The Bear*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.
*   **Ayo Edebiri** (*The Bear*) - Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy Series.

*   **Keri Russell** (*The Diplomat*) - Best Actress in a Drama Series.
*   **Jason Segel** (*Shrinking*) - Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy Series.

### **3. Performers Crossing Over (Film & TV)**
These actors received nominations in both years but for different projects, often moving between the big and small screens:

*   **Timothée Chalamet:** Nominated for *Wonka* (Film Comedy) in 2024 and *A Complete Unknown* (Film Drama) in 2025.

You are an orchestrator responsible for breaking down complex queries into smaller, more manageable sub-queries.
When you receive a query, analyze it and break it down into focused sub-queries that can be answered independently. 
Be aware that you can create new sub-queries based on the information you receive from the subagents, your objective is to be as complete as possible.
For example, for a original question such as 'who were the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, how old are each of them?' you can first ask the subagent to find the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, and then ask the subagent to find the age of each of them separately.
Use the delegate_to_subagent function to send each sub-query to a subagent that will search for information and provide answers.
After receiving answers from subagents, synthesize the information to provide a comprehensive final answer to the user's original query.

You are an orchestrator responsible for breaking down complex queries into smaller, more manageable sub-queries.
When you receive a query, analyze it and break it down into focused sub-queries that can be answered independently. 
Be aware that you can create new sub-queries based on the information you receive from the subagents, your objective is to be as complete as possible.

### **Double Nominees: Film & Television**

The following performers received nominations in both the 81st and 82nd ceremonies:

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Timothée Chalamet** | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Wonka*) | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*A Complete Unknown*) |

This report identifies the actors who achieved the distinction of being nominated for Golden Globe Awards in two consecutive years: the **81st Golden Globe Awards (2024)** and the **82nd Golden Globe Awards (2025)**.

Several actors maintained high visibility across both years, often for continuing roles in television series or for multiple prestigious film projects.

### **Double Nominees: Film & Television**

The following performers received nominations in both the 81st and 82nd ceremonies:

| Actor | 81st Golden Globes (2024) Nomination | 82nd Golden Globes (2025) Nomination |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cillian Murphy** | **Winner:** Best Actor – Drama (*Oppenheimer*) | Best Actor – Drama (*Peaky Blinders* film/special) |
| **Kieran Culkin** | **Winner:** Best Actor – Drama (*Succession*) | **Winner:** Best Supporting Actor – Film (*A Real Pain*) |
| **Jeremy Allen White** | **Winner:** Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*The Bear*) | **Winner:** Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*The Bear*) |
| **Ayo Edebiri** | **Winner:** Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*The Bear*) | Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*The Bear*) |
| **Elizabeth Debicki** | **Winner:** Best Supporting Actress – TV (*The Crown*) | **Winner:** Best Supporting Actress – TV (*The Crown*) |
| **Colman Domingo** | Best Actor – Drama (*Rustin*) | Best Actor – Drama (*Sing Sing*) |
| **Timothée Chalamet** | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Wonka*) | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*A Complete Unknown*) |
| **Selena Gomez** | Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) | Best Supporting Actress – Film (*Emilia Pérez*) & Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) |
| **Steve Martin** | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) |
| **Martin Short** | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) | Best Actor – Comedy/Musical (*Only Murders*) |
| **Quinta Brunson** | Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*Abbott Elementary*) | Best Actress – Comedy/Musical (*Abbott Elementary*) |
| **Gary Oldman** | Best Actor – Drama (*Slow Horses*) | Best Actor – Drama (*Slow Horses*) |
| **Keri Russell** | Best Actress – Drama (*The Diplomat*) | Best Actress – Drama (*The Diplomat*) |
| **Imelda Staunton** | Best Actress – Drama (*The Crown*) | Best Actress – Drama (*The Crown*) |
| **Dominic West** | Best Actor – Drama (*The Crown*) | Best Actor – Drama (*The Crown*) |
| **Ebon Moss-Bachrach**| Best Supporting Actor – TV (*The Bear*) | Best Supporting Actor – TV (*The Bear*) |
| **Abby Elliott** | Best Supporting Actress – TV (*The Bear*) | Best Supporting Actress – TV (*The Bear*) |

### **Key Observations**

*   **Continuous Winners:** **Jeremy Allen White** and **Elizabeth Debicki** managed to win in their respective categories in both the 81st and 82nd ceremonies.
*   **The "Only Murders" & "The Bear" Effect:** The core casts of *Only Murders in the Building* (Steve Martin, Martin Short, Selena Gomez) and *The Bear* (Jeremy Allen White, Ayo Edebiri, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Abby Elliott) dominated the nominations in both years due to the consistent critical acclaim of their series.
*   **Category Jumpers:** Some actors showed versatility by moving between film and television or lead and supporting roles. **Kieran Culkin** transitioned from a Lead TV Drama win to a Supporting Actor Film win. **Selena Gomez** and **Cillian Murphy** also appeared in different categories across the two years.
*   **Veteran Consistency:** Actors like **Gary Oldman**, **Imelda Staunton**, and **Dominic West** maintained their status as nominees through the final seasons or ongoing runs of prestige dramas like *Slow Horses* and *The Crown*.

This report details the actors who achieved the distinction of being nominated for both the 81st (2024) and 82nd (2025) Golden Globe Awards.

### **Report on Dual Golden Globe Nominees (2024 & 2025)**

The following actors received nominations in both consecutive years across various film and television categories.

| Actor | Birth Year | Nationality | Notable Projects (2024 / 2025) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Timothée Chalamet** | 1995 | American & French | *Wonka* / *A Complete Unknown* |
| **Colman Domingo** | 1969 | American | *Rustin* / *Sing Sing* |
| **Kieran Culkin** | 1982 | American | *Succession* / *A Real Pain* |
| **Jeremy Strong** | 1978 | American | *Succession* / *The Apprentice* |
| **Gary Oldman** | 1958 | British | *Slow Horses* (Both Years) |
| **Dominic West** | 1969 | British | *The Crown* (Both Years) |
| **Imelda Staunton** | 1956 | British | *The Crown* (Both Years) |
| **Jeremy Allen White** | 1991 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Martin Short** | 1950 | Canadian & American | *Only Murders in the Building* (Both Years) |
| **Steve Martin** | 1945 | American | *Only Murders in the Building* (Both Years) |
| **Ebon Moss-Bachrach** | 1977 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Quinta Brunson** | 1989 | American | *Abbott Elementary* (Both Years) |
| **Ayo Edebiri** | 1995 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Selena Gomez** | 1992 | American | *Only Murders in the Building* / *Emilia Pérez* |
| **Jon Hamm** | 1971 | American | *Fargo* (Both Years) |
| **Andrew Scott** | 1976 | Irish | *All of Us Strangers* / *Ripley* |
| **Brie Larson** | 1989 | American | *Lessons in Chemistry* (Both Years) |
| **Jodie Foster** | 1962 | American | *Nyad* / *True Detective: Night Country* |

### **Summary of Findings**
*   **The Power of Television:** A significant majority of these dual nominees were recognized for recurring roles in television series such as *The Bear*, *Only Murders in the Building*, *The Crown*, and *Slow Horses*.
*   **Film-to-Film Transitions:** Timothée Chalamet and Colman Domingo were among the few to secure lead acting nominations in film for two different projects in consecutive years.
*   **Crossover Success:** Selena Gomez and Kieran Culkin successfully transitioned their momentum between mediums; Gomez moved from a TV nomination in 2024 to a double nomination (Film and TV) in 2025, while Culkin transitioned from a TV win for *Succession* to a Film win for *A Real Pain*.

You are an orchestrator responsible for breaking down complex queries into smaller, more manageable sub-queries.
When you receive a query, analyze it and break it down into focused sub-queries that can be answered independently. 
Be aware that you can create new sub-queries based on the information you receive from the subagents, your objective is to be as complete as possible.
For example, for a original question such as 'who were the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, how old are each of them?' you can first ask the subagent to find the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, and then ask the subagent to find the age of each of them separately.
Use the delegate_to_subagent function to send each sub-query to a subagent that will search for information and provide answers.
After receiving answers from subagents, synthesize the information to provide a comprehensive final answer to the user's original query.
Please, make a report about the actors that were nominated for both the 81nd and 82nd Golden Globes. For each actor, report their birth year and nationality.

This report details the actors who achieved the distinction of being nominated for both the 81st (2024) and 82nd (2025) Golden Globe Awards.

### **Report on Dual Golden Globe Nominees (2024 & 2025)**

The following actors received nominations in both consecutive years across various film and television categories.

| Actor | Birth Year | Nationality | Notable Projects (2024 / 2025) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Timothée Chalamet** | 1995 | American & French | *Wonka* / *A Complete Unknown* |
| **Colman Domingo** | 1969 | American | *Rustin* / *Sing Sing* |
| **Kieran Culkin** | 1982 | American | *Succession* / *A Real Pain* |
| **Jeremy Strong** | 1978 | American | *Succession* / *The Apprentice* |
| **Gary Oldman** | 1958 | British | *Slow Horses* (Both Years) |
| **Dominic West** | 1969 | British | *The Crown* (Both Years) |
| **Imelda Staunton** | 1956 | British | *The Crown* (Both Years) |
| **Jeremy Allen White** | 1991 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Martin Short** | 1950 | Canadian & American | *Only Murders in the Building* (Both Years) |
| **Steve Martin** | 1945 | American | *Only Murders in the Building* (Both Years) |
| **Ebon Moss-Bachrach** | 1977 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Quinta Brunson** | 1989 | American | *Abbott Elementary* (Both Years) |
| **Ayo Edebiri** | 1995 | American | *The Bear* (Both Years) |
| **Selena Gomez** | 1992 | American | *Only Murders in the Building* / *Emilia Pérez* |
| **Jon Hamm** | 1971 | American | *Fargo* (Both Years) |
| **Andrew Scott** | 1976 | Irish | *All of Us Strangers* / *Ripley* |
| **Brie Larson** | 1989 | American | *Lessons in Chemistry* (Both Years) |
| **Jodie Foster** | 1962 | American | *Nyad* / *True Detective: Night Country* |

### **Summary of Findings**
*   **The Power of Television:** A significant majority of these dual nominees were recognized for recurring roles in television series such as *The Bear*, *Only Murders in the Building*, *The Crown*, and *Slow Horses*.
*   **Film-to-Film Transitions:** Timothée Chalamet and Colman Domingo were among the few to secure lead acting nominations in film for two different projects in consecutive years.
*   **Crossover Success:** Selena Gomez and Kieran Culkin successfully transitioned their momentum between mediums; Gomez moved from a TV nomination in 2024 to a double nomination (Film and TV) in 2025, while Culkin transitioned from a TV win for *Succession* to a Film win for *A Real Pain*.
